---
title: "Should I amend my soil?"
description: "Before you buy compost, topsoil or sand, check whether your soil needs it. A free decision tool from soil scientists, for lawns, vegetable beds, shrubs, trees and native plants."
anchor-sections: false
include-in-header: _hm-head.html
---

Compost and topsoil are useful, but a lot of money goes on amendments that don't help, or make things worse. Answer a few questions and this tells you what's worth doing for what you're planting.

```{=html}
<div class="hmc" id="am"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  HM.tool({
    id: 'am', step: 'What you\'re planting', units: false,
    inputs: [
      { k: 'plant', l: 'Planting', t: 'select', d: 'veg', opts: [['veg', 'Vegetable or fruit bed'], ['beds', 'Flower beds or shrubs'], ['native', 'Native or low-water plants'], ['tree', 'Planting a tree or shrub (the planting hole)'], ['newlawn', 'New lawn (seed or sod)'], ['lawn', 'Improving an existing lawn']] },
      { t: 'sec', l: 'Your soil', h: 'Answer what you can. <a href="diy-soil-tests.qmd">DIY soil tests</a> help with texture and drainage.' },
      { k: 'om', l: 'Organic matter (from a soil test)', t: 'select', d: 'unk', opts: [['unk', 'Don\'t know'], ['low', 'Under 2%'], ['mid', '2–5%'], ['high', 'Over 5%']] },
      { k: 'tex', l: 'Texture', t: 'select', d: 'unk', opts: [['unk', 'Don\'t know'], ['sand', 'Sandy (gritty, falls apart)'], ['loam', 'Loamy (in between)'], ['clay', 'Clay (sticky when wet, hard when dry)']] },
      { k: 'drain', l: 'After heavy rain or a drainage test, water…', t: 'select', d: 'unk', opts: [['unk', 'Don\'t know'], ['ok', 'Drains within a few hours'], ['slow', 'Puddles for most of a day'], ['bad', 'Stands for more than a day']] },
      { k: 'comp', l: 'A screwdriver is hard to push in more than 2–3 in when the soil is moist', t: 'check', d: false },
      { k: 'new', l: 'The house or yard was built or regraded in the last few years', t: 'check', d: false }
    ],
    compute(v, U) {
      const P = v.plant, low = v.om === 'low', high = v.om === 'high', unk = v.om === 'unk';
      const doL = [], dontL = [];
      let verdict, sub, cls = '';
      // blockers first
      if (v.drain === 'bad') {
        verdict = 'Fix drainage first'; sub = 'Standing water is caused by what\'s below, usually a compacted or dense layer, or water flowing in from elsewhere. No amendment mixed into the top few inches will fix it.'; cls = 'bad';
        doL.push('Dig a test hole to find out why: a hard layer you can break up, or water arriving from a downspout or slope you can redirect.', 'Consider raised beds, regrading, a <a href="rain-garden.qmd">rain garden</a>, or plants that tolerate wet roots.');
      }
      if (v.comp || v.new) {
        doL.push(P === 'lawn' ? 'Core aerate (pull plugs) when the soil is moist; repeat yearly until the screwdriver goes in easily.' : 'Loosen compacted soil first, as deep and wide as you can (8–12 in for beds), before adding anything.');
        if (v.new) doL.push('New-build lots often have thin topsoil over compacted subsoil. The <a href="construction-soil-check.qmd">construction soil check</a> walks through it.');
      }
      if (P === 'tree') {
        verdict = verdict || 'Don\'t amend the planting hole'; sub = sub || 'Roots grow best when the hole is backfilled with the soil that came out of it. Rich backfill acts like a pot: water collects in it and roots circle instead of spreading.';
        doL.push('Dig the hole 2–3 times as wide as the root ball but no deeper, so the root flare sits at or slightly above grade.', 'Backfill with the native soil, water it in, and spread 2–4 in of mulch over a wide circle, kept off the trunk.');
        dontL.push('Compost, potting mix or topsoil in the planting hole.', 'Gravel in the bottom of the hole: it makes drainage worse, not better.');
      } else if (P === 'native') {
        verdict = verdict || 'Probably not'; sub = sub || 'Native and low-water plants are adapted to unimproved soil. Rich, amended soil often makes them floppy, short-lived and weedier.';
        dontL.push('Compost or topsoil "to give them a good start", unless the soil is badly disturbed fill.');
        doL.push('Loosen compacted soil, plant, and mulch with gravel or a thin layer of wood chips (as the plants prefer).');
      } else if (P === 'veg') {
        if (high) { verdict = verdict || 'Not much'; sub = sub || 'Your organic matter is already high. A thin top-up keeps it there.'; doL.push('Spread about ½ in of compost each year, or grow a cover crop.'); dontL.push('Large compost or topsoil deliveries.'); }
        else { verdict = verdict || 'Yes: compost'; sub = sub || 'Vegetables do best in soil with plenty of organic matter (around 5% or more).'; cls = cls || 'good'; doL.push(`Mix ${low || unk ? '2' : '1'} in of compost into the top 6–8 in each year. One inch over 1,000 ft² is about 3 cubic yards: the <a href="materials-calculator.qmd?m=compost">materials calculator</a> does the sum.`); }
      } else if (P === 'beds') {
        if (high) { verdict = verdict || 'No'; sub = sub || 'Organic matter is already high.'; dontL.push('Compost or soil conditioner.'); doL.push('Just mulch: as it breaks down it feeds the soil.'); }
        else if (low) { verdict = verdict || 'Once, then mulch'; sub = sub || 'Low organic matter is worth fixing once when you make the bed.'; cls = cls || 'good'; doL.push('Mix 1–2 in of compost into the top 8 in when you make the bed, then keep it mulched.'); }
        else { verdict = verdict || 'Optional'; sub = sub || 'Most shrubs and perennials grow well in ordinary soil.'; doL.push('If you add anything, ½–1 in of compost mixed in when planting is plenty. Mulch does the rest over time.'); }
      } else if (P === 'newlawn') {
        if (low || unk || v.comp || v.new) { verdict = verdict || 'Yes, before seeding'; sub = sub || 'This is your one chance to improve the soil under a lawn.'; cls = cls || 'good'; doL.push('Loosen the top 6 in and mix in about 1 in of compost (about 3 cubic yards per 1,000 ft²) before seeding or laying sod.'); }
        else { verdict = verdict || 'Probably not'; sub = sub || 'Your soil already has reasonable organic matter.'; doL.push('Loosen the top few inches, level, and seed or sod.'); }
        dontL.push('A thin layer of topsoil over compacted ground: it creates a layer roots won\'t cross. Loosen first and mix it in.');
      } else if (P === 'lawn') {
        verdict = verdict || (low || unk ? 'A light top-dress' : 'Not much'); sub = sub || 'You can\'t mix anything into an existing lawn, so improve it from the top.';
        doL.push('Core aerate, then top-dress with ¼ in of fine compost and rake it into the holes. Repeat yearly.');
        dontL.push('Spreading inches of topsoil over the grass: it smothers the turf and creates a layer.');
      }
      if (v.tex === 'clay' && (P === 'tree' || P === 'native')) dontL.push('Sand to "loosen" clay: it fills the gaps and makes clay denser.');
      if (v.tex === 'clay' && P !== 'tree' && P !== 'native') { dontL.push('Sand to "loosen" clay: unless it makes up over half the mix, sand fills the gaps and makes clay denser, closer to concrete.'); doL.push('For clay, compost and not walking or digging on it when wet are what improve structure.'); }
      if (v.tex === 'sand' && P !== 'native' && P !== 'tree') doL.push('Sandy soil gains most from compost: it holds water and nutrients the sand can\'t.');
      dontL.push('Gypsum, unless a lab test shows sodium. It doesn\'t loosen ordinary clay.');
      return U.big('Verdict', verdict, sub) + `<h3>Worth doing</h3><ul class="plain">${doL.map(x => `<li>${x}</li>`).join('')}</ul>` + (dontL.length ? `<h3>Skip</h3><ul class="plain">${dontL.map(x => `<li>${x}</li>`).join('')}</ul>` : '') +
        (unk && P !== 'tree' && P !== 'native' ? U.note('A <a href="soil-test-translator.qmd">soil test</a> would firm this up: organic matter is the key number.') : '');
    }
  });
})();
</script>
```

## The short version

- **Trees:** never amend the planting hole. Wide hole, native soil, mulch.
- **Native and low-water plants:** usually nothing. Rich soil works against them.
- **Vegetables:** yes, compost every year.
- **Lawns:** improve the soil before seeding. On an existing lawn, aerate and top-dress lightly.
- **Clay:** compost helps; a little sand makes it worse.
- **Standing water:** a drainage problem, not a soil-quality one.
